title: Why Paying by Card Doubles What You Spend (MIT Study)
alt_title_1: The MIT Basketball Ticket Test Every Spender Should Know
alt_title_2: How Tap-to-Pay Tricks Your Brain Into Paying Twice as Much
description_hook: In 2001, MIT professors Drazen Prelec and Duncan Simester auctioned real sold-out Boston Celtics tickets to MBA students. Students paying by credit card bid $60.64 on average, while cash bidders stopped at $28.51. Source: Marketing Letters, Vol. 12, No. 1 (2001).

scenes.headline: The MIT Sold-Out NBA Ticket Experiment
scenes.stat_label: HIGHER BIDS FOR THE EXACT SAME SEATS
bullets: Real sealed-bid auction for sold-out Celtics tickets
Only one rule changed between the two student groups
scenes.narration: In 2001, two MIT professors auctioned sold-out Boston Celtics tickets to MBA students, and one rule made half the room bid twice as much.
scenes.source: Drazen Prelec & Duncan Simester, Marketing Letters (2001)

scenes.headline: Cash Within 24 Hours vs Credit Card
scenes.left_body: Average bid: $28.51 paid in physical bills
scenes.narration: Students paying cash within twenty-four hours bid an average of twenty-eight dollars and fifty-one cents. Students paying by credit card bid sixty dollars and sixty-four cents.
scenes.source: Prelec & Simester, MIT Sloan Auction Data (2001)

scenes.headline: Why Tap-to-Pay Numbs the Pain Center
scenes.stat_label: SILENT MARKUP FROM PAYMENT FRICTION LOSS
bullets: Handing over bills triggers immediate loss awareness
Tapping a phone delays the mental cost by 30 days
scenes.narration: Economists call this the pain of paying. Cash makes your brain feel the loss right now. A card delivers the reward today and hides the bill next month.

scenes.headline: Convert Price Tags Into Net Work Hours
scenes.stat_subtext: $90 Impulse Buy at $22.50/hr Net = 4 Hours of Life
scenes.narration: Before tapping for any non-essential item, divide its price by your net hourly pay. At twenty-two fifty an hour, a ninety-dollar impulse buy costs four desk hours.

scenes.headline: Put Friction Back Before You Tap
scenes.stat_label: WAIT RULE FOR ANY PURCHASE OVER 2 WORK HOURS
bullets: Wait 24 hours whenever an item costs over 2 work hours
Keep the cash gap working in your own account
scenes.narration: Wait twenty-four hours on anything above two work hours, and you stop overpaying like the credit card half of that MIT room.
